# A Website Is Just Files

## Meet Dr. Mabel Hatter

-   Download [`hatter_site.zip`](hatter_site.zip), and unzip it into `classwork/day_35/`.
-   Open `index.html` in your browser.
-   Click around: Home, CV, Research.

## What's in the Folder?

```
hatter_site/
├── index.html      ← the homepage
├── cv.html         ← the CV page
├── research.html   ← the research page
├── style.css       ← how everything looks (Wednesday!)
└── teacup.svg      ← a picture
```

-   A website is a **folder of text files**.
-   Your browser reads them and turns them into what you see.

## Two Ways to Look at a Page

1.  **The browser** shows you the page.
2.  **VS Code** shows you the code behind it.

-   Open `index.html` in VS Code, too. Put the two windows side by side.
-   Find *Dr. Mabel Hatter* in both.

# Hunt 1: Text

## Hunt 1: `index.html`, `cv.html`

1.  Find `<p>` and `</p>`. What's the difference between them? What's *between* them?
2.  *Dr. Mabel Hatter* and *About Me* are both headings. What tags make them?
3.  Find the **bold** words and the *italic* word on the homepage. What makes them bold and italic?

## Hunt 1: `index.html`, `cv.html`
4.  *Contact* has a bulleted list; *Publications* on the CV has a numbered list. What's different in the code?
5.  Find the *Teaching* table on the CV. List every tag it uses, and guess what each one stands for.
6.  Change `<h2>About Me</h2>` to `<h3>About Me</h3>`. Save and reload. What changes? (Then change it back.)

## Tags Mark Up Text

```html
<p>I study how people talk at tea parties.</p>
```

-   `<p>` is an **opening tag**; `</p>` is a **closing tag** (with a `/`).
-   Together with the text between them, they make an **element**.
-   `p` means **paragraph**.

## Tags Inside Tags

```html
<p>My research uses Python to analyze <em>conversation</em> in literature.</p>
```

-   `<em>` (**emphasis**) is *inside* the `<p>`: it makes *conversation* italic.
-   Tags **nest**: the inner one has to close before the outer one.

## Lists

```html
<ul>                                <ol>
  <li>Office: ...</li>                <li>Hatter, M. (2025)...</li>
  <li>Office hours: ...</li>          <li>Hatter, M. &amp; Hare, M. (2023)...</li>
</ul>                               </ol>
```

-   `<ul>`: **unordered** list (bullets); `<ol>`: **ordered** list (numbers)
-   Each item is an `<li>` (**list item**), either way.
-   With `<ol>`, the browser does the numbering for you.

## Tables

```html
<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Course</th>
    <th>Title</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>LIN 101</td>
    <td>Introduction to Nonsense</td>
  </tr>
</table>
```

-   `<tr>`: a **table row**
-   `<th>`: a **table header** cell; `<td>`: a **table data** cell
-   A table is built **row by row**, like a list of lists in Python.

## Hunt 1: Possible Answer

1.  `</p>` has a `/`: it **closes** the paragraph. The text in between is what you see.
2.  `<h1>Dr. Mabel Hatter</h1>` and `<h2>About Me</h2>`: `h1` is the biggest.
3.  `<strong>` for bold, `<em>` for italic
4.  `<ul>` vs. `<ol>`; the items are `<li>` in both.
5.  `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, `<td>`
6.  *About Me* gets smaller, and loses its purple line. (Why? We'll see on Wednesday!)

## Common Tags

| Tag | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<h1>`, `<h2>`, `<h3>` | headings (1 is the biggest) |
| `<p>` | a paragraph |
| `<strong>`, `<em>` | bold, italic |
| `<ul>`, `<ol>`, `<li>` | bulleted list, numbered list, list item |
| `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, `<td>` | table, row, header cell, cell |

# Hunt 2: Links and Pictures

## Hunt 2: `index.html`, `cv.html`

1.  Find the three links in the navigation bar (*Home*, *CV*, *Research*). What do they have in common?
2.  Find the link to *Project Gutenberg* on the research page. How is it different from the navigation links?
3.  Find Dr. Hatter's email address. What happens when you click it? What in the code makes that happen?

## Hunt 2: `index.html`, `cv.html`

4.  Find the teacup. Which part of the code says *which* picture to show?
5.  The teacup's code has a second part, with a description in it. Change `teacup.svg` to `teapot.svg`, save, and reload. When does the description show up?
6.  Every tag so far has had a closing tag. Which one doesn't? Why not?

## Tags Can Carry Information

```html
<a href="cv.html">CV</a>
```

-   `<a>` makes a **link** (*a* for **anchor**).
-   `href="cv.html"` is an **attribute**: it says *where* the link goes.
-   Attributes go **inside** the opening tag: `name="value"`

## Three Kinds of Links

```html
<a href="cv.html">CV</a>
<a href="https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11">Project Gutenberg</a>
<a href="mailto:mhatter@wonderland.example">mhatter@wonderland.example</a>
```

-   `cv.html`: another file in the **same folder**
-   `https://...`: a page on **another website**
-   `mailto:`: opens an **email**

## Images

```html
<img src="teacup.svg" alt="A drawing of a steaming teacup">
```

-   `src`: the image **file** (**source**)
-   `alt`: a **description**, for screen readers and for when the image doesn't load
-   `<img>` has **no closing tag**: there's no text inside it.

## Hunt 2: Possible Answer

1.  They're all `<a href="...">`, and each `href` is a file in the **same folder**.
2.  Its `href` starts with `https://`: it's on **another website**.
3.  Your email program opens: `href="mailto:..."`
4.  `src="teacup.svg"`
5.  The picture disappears, and the `alt` text shows up instead.
6.  `<img>`: there's no text to wrap, so there's nothing to close.

# Hunt 3: The Shape of a Page

## Hunt 3: all three `.html` files

1.  Look at the **tab** at the top of your browser window: it says *Dr. Mabel Hatter*. Click over to the CV: what does the tab say now? Find where that text comes from in the code. Is it inside `<body>`?
2.  Find something between `<!--` and `-->`. Does it show up on the page?
3.  Find `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, and `<footer>`. Which ones are **inside** which?

## Hunt 3: all three `.html` files

4.  In the browser, **right-click** on *About Me* and choose **Inspect**. Hover over the lines in the panel that opens. What happens?
5.  Compare `index.html`, `cv.html`, and `research.html`. Which parts are **exactly the same** in all three?

## The Skeleton

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>Dr. Mabel Hatter</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>
  ...everything you see...
</body>
</html>
```

-   `<head>`: information **about** the page (the title in the browser tab, the stylesheet)
-   `<body>`: everything you **see**

## Comments

```html
<!-- The BODY holds everything you see. -->
```

-   Anything between `<!--` and `-->` is a **comment**: notes for people, ignored by the browser.
-   Just like `#` in Python.

## Boxes Inside Boxes

```html
<body>
  <header>
    <h1>Dr. Mabel Hatter</h1>
    <nav> ...the links... </nav>
  </header>
  <main> ...the content... </main>
  <footer> ...the copyright line... </footer>
</body>
```

-   `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`: tags that say what **part** of the page something is
-   The **indentation** shows the nesting -- like a syntax tree!

## Inspect Element

-   **Right-click → Inspect** works on **any** website, not just Dr. Hatter's.
-   The browser shows you the element, and every box it's inside.
-   Hovering over a line highlights that box on the page.

## Hunt 3: Possible Answer

1.  `<title>`, inside `<head>`, not `<body>`
2.  Comments never show up on the page.
3.  `<nav>` is inside `<header>`; `<header>`, `<main>`, and `<footer>` are all inside `<body>`.
4.  The browser highlights each box on the page.
5.  The `<head>` (except the `<title>`), the whole `<header>` and `<nav>`, and the `<footer>`: they're **copied** into every page.

# Your Turn

## A Home for Your Website

1.  On GitHub, make a new **public** repository named exactly `your-username.github.io`, with your GitHub username, in lowercase. Check **Add a README**.
2.  In VS Code: Command Palette → **Git: Clone** → paste its URL. Put it in your `computation_4_linguists` folder, **next to** `LIN_301/`, not inside it.
3.  Copy `style.css` and `teacup.svg` from `hatter_site/` into your new repo. (Dr. Hatter's style for now: on Wednesday, you'll learn how to change it.)

## Build Your Own Homepage

-   In your new repo, make a **new, empty** file: `index.html`. (It has to be called `index.html`: that's the page GitHub shows first.)
-   Write it **by hand**. You can look at Dr. Hatter's files as much as you like, but don't copy and paste the whole thing!
-   Everything you push here is **public**: use your UK email, and no phone number or address.

## Your Homepage Needs...

From **Hunt 3**:

-   the skeleton: `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<head>`, `<body>`
-   a `<title>` with your name, and the `<link>` to `style.css`
-   a `<header>`, a `<main>`, and a `<footer>`
-   at least one comment

## ...and...

From **Hunts 1 and 2**:

-   an `<h1>` with your name
-   a `<nav>` with links to `index.html`, `cv.html`, and `research.html`
-   at least two `<h2>` sections (*About Me*, *Contact*, *Interests*...)
-   a paragraph with something in `<strong>` and something in `<em>`
-   a bulleted list
-   a link to **another website**, and an email link
-   a picture, with `alt` text (`teacup.svg` is fine for now!)

## Check Your Work

-   Open your `index.html` in your browser. Does it look the way you expected?
-   **Inspect** it: are your boxes inside the boxes you meant?
-   Trade with your neighbor. Go down the checklist: what's missing from their page?
-   Then publish it!

## Publish It

1.  Commit and push:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "My first homepage"
git push
```

2.  On GitHub: **Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → `main` → `/ (root)`** → **Save**.

-   After a minute or two, your page is live at `https://your-username.github.io`!
-   Your *CV* and *Research* links lead to an error page for now. On Friday, you'll fill them in.

## If You Finish Early

1.  Make `cv.html`, with an `<ol>` and a `<table>`. (Hint: copy *your* `index.html`, and change the `<main>`.) Push it: does your *CV* link work now?
2.  Make `teaching.html`, and add a *Teaching* link to the navigation bar.
3.  Does your new link show up on **every** page? Why not?

## If You Finish Early: Possible Answer

-   The navigation bar is **copied** into every page. To add a link, you have to edit **every** file!
-   On Friday, Quarto will fix this: you'll write the navigation bar **once**.
-   What you wrote about yourself today is a first draft of your HW 8 homepage: on Friday, it moves into Quarto, in this same repo.

# Looking Ahead

## What Did We Learn Today?

-   A website is a folder of **text files**.
-   **Tags** mark up text: `<h1>`, `<p>`, `<ul>`, `<li>`, `<table>`...
-   **Attributes** add information: `href`, `src`, `alt`
-   `<head>` vs. `<body>`; boxes inside boxes
-   **Inspect Element** shows you how any page is built.
